data.narrative:
Peak Energy is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Landon Mossburg and Liam O'Connor that has raised $65M to date. The valuation landscape includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers in the Climate & Energy sector, though none cluster tightly around Peak's stage and valuation tier.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach here. Using total raised ($65M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series A-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied valuation of $130M. The peer-median method is not actionable: while eight same-sector peers exist, none meet the narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier simultaneously. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material noise given the heterogeneity of climate tech business models.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $110M to $150M, with a median point of $130M, grounded in a single method. Key uncertainties include the appropriate step-up multiplier for Peak's specific risk profile, capital efficiency relative to sector peers, and the absence of a tighter peer set at Series A stage within Climate & Energy. Any valuation below $110M or above $150M would require external validation (e.g., recent institutional rounds, material revenue traction, or sector-specific benchmarks not present in this dataset).
